workload: One public text-only opportunity exchange. Model has no tools.

response.decision: No pilot is warranted at this stage due to insufficient evidence of distinct performance advantages or cost-effectiveness of self-hosted coding systems under mean charged-token constraints. The available records do not provide issue-level, model-specific, or cost-accurate comparisons that would allow for independent acceptance of a private repository maintenance pilot.
response.incumbent: Existing open-source harnesses (e.g., those evaluated by Zhao et al.) with proven performance on verified SWE-bench issues under common serving conditions represent a stronger, more reliable baseline.
limitations: No record provides direct comparison of self-hosted systems against hosted alternatives on token cost or issue resolution under bounded charging.
All performance claims are aggregated or model-agnostic; no issue-level breakdowns exist for self-hosted systems.
Missing data on token usage patterns (e.g., caching, repetition) in self-hosted environments prevents accurate cost modeling.
No evidence of private backlog or operational overheads in self-hosted systems that would justify pilot costs.

opportunities.move: Conduct a targeted analysis of Figshare v1’s issue-level outcomes to identify patterns in failure rates and token usage across models, then use those to benchmark against known open-source harnesses. This would establish a baseline for what constitutes a 'performance gap' under token constraints.
opportunities.title: Issue-level token and failure pattern analysis from public benchmark data

opportunities.move: Re-examine Zhao, Poskitt and Lo’s findings to isolate the harness that achieved a 44% improvement in resolution and evaluate whether it operates efficiently under token budgeting. This could inform whether any lightweight model-harness pairing is viable without hosting overhead.
opportunities.title: Evaluation of high-resolution harness performance under token constraints

opportunities.move: Synthesize Fan et al.’s context management findings to assess whether dynamic window budgeting or planning could improve efficiency in self-hosted agents, even without direct token cost data.
opportunities.title: Context-aware planning as a potential efficiency lever in self-hosted agents

opportunities.move: Use Srinivasan and Menzies’ trial acquisition data to model statistical uncertainty in agent performance under budget constraints, and assess whether any observed differences are robust or attributable to noise.
opportunities.title: Statistical validation of performance differences under budget constraints

opportunities.move: Propose a minimal pilot design that compares one lightweight coding model (e.g., from B) with a known open-source harness on a subset of 10 verified SWE-bench issues, using only public token records from Figshare (C) to estimate cost. This would test feasibility without committing to full private maintenance.
opportunities.title: Minimal feasibility pilot on a subset of verified issues

response.test: For any proposed self-hosted system, the smallest discriminating test is whether it resolves at least 90% of the issues in a 10-issue SWE-bench subset with a mean charged-token cost per issue that is 10% lower than the best open-source harness under identical conditions. This test must be grounded solely in public records and must not assume private data or operational control.
